answer: Harbor grants one berth per key. An applicant locks 60 credits, pays a fee, and posts a crystal seal, a hash of its key, berth, and epoch, to the glacier archive for public recomputation against duplicates and reused seals. The fee is 25 credits for the first 400 berths, 40 for the next 400, 60 beyond 800. One fake costs 85 credits, rising to 120; 1000 fakes lock 60,000 and pay 38,000 in fees, 98,000 total. A berth-rental ring fails: a rented seal mismatches the renter's key, so harbor rejects it and burns the bond. An honest operator pays one set and recovers its bond after one clean epoch.
